title: Unramified morphisms are stable under base change and restriction to opens
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be an unramified morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. (1) For every morphism $g:S'\to S$ of schemes, the base change $f':X\times_S S'\to S'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is unramified. (2) If $U\subseteq X$ and $V\subseteq S$ are open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion] with $f(U)\subseteq V$, then the restriction $f|_U:U\to V$ is unramified. (Stacks Project, Tags [02GA] and [02G6].)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02GA (lemma-base-change-unramified, morphisms.tex lines 7717-7730) for (1) and the final 'Moreover' clause of Lemma 02G6 (lemma-unramified-characterize, lines 7668-7697) for (2)

proof.text: *(1), finite type.* Let $f:X\to S$ be unramified and $g:S'\to S$ a morphism; write $X'=X\times_SS'$ and $f':X'\to S'$ for the second projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. By [def-weil-unramified-morphism], $f$ is locally of finite type, so $f'$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change].

*(1), formally unramified.* Since $f$ is unramified it is formally unramified by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-formally-unramified] [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism], and hence its base change $f':X'\to S'$ is formally unramified by [lem-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-base-change].

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02HE (lemma-unramified-formally-unramified), (1) implies (2), and Lemma 02HB (lemma-base-change-formally-unramified)

proof.text: *(1), conclusion.* By steps 1 and 2, $f'$ is locally of finite type and formally unramified, so it is unramified by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-formally-unramified-unramified]. This proves (1).

*(2), finite type.* Let $U\subseteq X$, $V\subseteq S$ be open subschemes with $f(U)\subseteq V$, with inclusions $j:U\to X$, $k:V\to S$ (open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]), and let $f|_U:U\to V$ be the restriction, the unique morphism with $k\circ f|_U=f\circ j$. Let $V'\subseteq V$ and $U'\subseteq U$ be affine opens with $f|_U(U')\subseteq V'$. Then $V'$ and $U'$ are affine opens of $S$ and $X$ with $f(U')\subseteq V'$, and $\mathcal O_V(V')=\mathcal O_S(V')$, $\mathcal O_U(U')=\mathcal O_X(U')$ with the same ring map $\mathcal O_S(V')\to\mathcal O_X(U')$ induced by $f$ and by $f|_U$. Since $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-unramified-morphism], this ring map is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] (only if); as $U'$, $V'$ were arbitrary, $f|_U$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] (if).

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize), final 'Moreover' clause (lines 2690-2692), proved via (1)<=>(2)

proof.text:
*(2), formally unramified.* $f$ is formally unramified by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-formally-unramified]. Let $T\subset T'$ be a first order thickening of affine schemes over $V$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], with closed immersion $i:T	o T'$ and structure morphism $b:T'	o V$, let $a:T	o U$ with $f|_U\circ a=b\circ i$, and let $a'_1,a'_2:T'	o U$ with $f|_U\circ a'_
u=b$ and $a'_
u\circ i=a$ ($
u=1,2$). Via $k\circ b:T'	o S$ the same $T\subset T'$ is a first order thickening of affine schemes over $S$; the morphism $j\circ a:T	o X$ is over $S$ ($f\circ j\circ a=k\circ f|_U\circ a=k\circ b\circ i$), and $j\circ a'_1$, $j\circ a'_2$ are morphisms $T'	o X$ over $S$ ($f\circ j\circ a'_
u=k\circ f|_U\circ a'_
u=k\circ b$) with $(j\circ a'_
u)\circ i=j\circ a$. By the definition of formally unramified [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism] applied to $f$, $j\circ a'_1=j\circ a'_2$, and since the open immersion $j$ is a monomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism], $a'_1=a'_2$. So $f|_U:U	o V$ is formally unramified [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism].

source.place: More on Morphisms, Definition 02H8 (definition-formally-unramified, line 798); argument written by the agent (Stacks proves the restriction clause of 02G6 through the locality of unramified ring maps instead)

proof.text: *(2), conclusion.* By steps 4 and 5, $f|_U:U\to V$ is locally of finite type and formally unramified, hence unramified by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-formally-unramified-unramified]. This proves (2).
